messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on gateway (region: us-west-2). Metric spike started at ~1861203000. Routing errors and timeouts increasing. Auto-paging: eng-runtime-oncall, maria-oncall
pagerduty: Paging eng-runtime-oncall (maria-oncall) — please acknowledge
maria-oncall: ACK. I'm on it. What do we have? CPU/GPU pressure or queueing?
eng-runtime-oncall: I'm looking at the scheduler dashboard — queuing/backlog growing on batching scheduler pool "batcher-ws". Head-of-line blocking visible: one long-lived batch is preventing progress.
sre-lead-jon: Can you grab the queue depth and oldest-in-queue age from /internal/metrics? Also error types (503 vs 504 vs 5xx from model backend)
eng-runtime-oncall: running: curl -s http://metrics.internal/batcher-ws | grep -E "queue_depth|oldest_age|batch_inflight"
eng-runtime-oncall: returned:
```
queue_depth 1342
oldest_age_seconds 78.32
batch_inflight 27
avg_batch_size 16.2
```
alex-platform: 1342 queue depth... that's way above expected. avg_batch_size 16 suggests big full batches. Could be long tail from a few requests with massive token counts.
lina-support: CS reports multiple customers seeing timeouts and 500s: Chatly (prod), DocFlow (staging->prod switched earlier), and internal demo endpoints. Customers complaining about 502/504 and interactive chat sessions dropping.
sam-mlops: Check KV cache pressure and model token length distribution. If a few requests have 4k+ tokens they can blow up batching.
noah-runtime: pulling logs from the batcher instances now. Grepping for stuck batches. Command:
```
kubectl logs -l app=batcher-ws -c batcher -n inference --since=5m | grep "stuck_batch" -n || true
```
noah-runtime: found repeated pattern: "batch_time_exceeded" and "backend_timeout: context deadline exceeded" about every 10-20s
eng-runtime-oncall: top-level symptom: gateway is returning 502/504 because scheduler waits to form large batch and some backends time out when batch triggers long compute or queue overflow.
sre-lead-jon: Immediate mitigation proposals (pick 1-2):
- Force smaller max_batch_size / reduce batch wait timeout to break head-of-line.
- Temporarily disable batching for affected route(s) and fall back to single-request mode (higher per-token cost but lower tail latency).
- Route traffic to fallback model variant (smaller / quantized) until backlog drains.
- Add temporary token-level rate limit per API key to throttle noisy callers.
maria-oncall: I'll reduce batch_wait_ms and max_batch_size for batcher-ws via feature flag. Doing change in config store now.
eng-runtime-oncall: config patch applied:
```
PATCH /configs/batcher-ws
{ "max_batch_size": 8, "batch_wait_ms": 20 }
```
maria-oncall: Rolling restart for batcher-ws config reload started across 4 nodes
devops-bot: Rolling restart started: batcher-ws (nodes 1/4)
noah-runtime: Observing queue depth after change...
(noah-runtime updates 30s later)
noah-runtime: queue_depth dropped from 1342 -> 480 in ~45s. oldest_age_seconds down from 78 -> 12. Error rate decreased from 6.2% -> 1.8% in gateway metrics.
lina-support: Noting customer reports improving, but Chatly still sees intermittent 502s for long running sessions.
sam-mlops: I'm going to enable route-based fallback for routes tagged "chat-interactive" to point to model "rwd-llm-small-v1" for 10% of traffic to validate correctness. Executing rollout.
eng-runtime-oncall: fallback rollout applied as canary 10% for chat-interactive routes
prod-paul: Notifying affected customers: draft message for CS review: "We're seeing transient elevated errors affecting interactive chat. We're mitigating by temporarily routing some traffic to a lower-latency model and reducing batch sizes. We'll share updates every 15 minutes." Lina please send.
lina-support: Sending now. CS notify to Chatly and DocFlow sent. PR docs updated with incident link and status.
sre-lead-jon: While the queue is draining, let's also look for root cause: why did batching suddenly form such large batches? Any recent deploys? Any users sending huge token counts?
alex-platform: I see a deploy to the client routing service 30m before the spike (deploy-2026-03-14-1150) which changed per-request prefill behavior — might have increased average request length due to adding context window. Checking.
noah-runtime: Correlating request size histograms pre/post deploy:
```
pre-deploy p95 tokens: 120
post-deploy p95 tokens: 1040
```
noah-runtime: huge jump — confirms deploy caused large token inputs for some clients.
sam-mlops: That explains avg_batch_size bump; clients with large tokens cause bigger batches and longer compute. We should revert that change or patch the client to limit token submission. Immediate action: add per-request token limit on gateway (hard cap 2048) and enforce 1s queue backoff for very long requests.
maria-oncall: Applying token cap rule on gateway ACLs now.
eng-runtime-oncall: Token cap rule pushed. Also enabled per-key rate limit for top 20 noisy API keys. That should stop full-throttle noisy clients.
devops-bot: Gateway config change completed (ruleset id: gw-186120-1)
noah-runtime: Metrics now: queue_depth trending to ~120, oldest_age_seconds < 5, error rate down to 0.5% in the last 2 minutes. Good.
lina-support: CS update: most customers reporting reduced errors. Chatly still has degraded sessions for ~5% of users; recommending they retry. Continuing to monitor and keep them updated.
product-paul: From product side, we'll open a follow-up for safer client/SDK defaults and guardrails to avoid sending massive contexts. Tagging devex and SDK teams.
sre-lead-jon: Next steps for incident:
- Continue monitoring for 30 minutes.
- Collect logs for postmortem and attach config diffs (batcher config, gateway rules).
- Add incident severity: Sev2 -> Upgrade to Sev1 if error rate climbs above 3% for >10min or more customers impacted.
- Handoff to night oncall (maria) in 25 minutes with runbook notes.
maria-oncall: I'm remaining as primary. If anything spikes again, escalate to jon and oncall exec.
alex-platform: Reverted the client-side prefill change in routing service (deploy rollback-2026-03-14-1215) to prevent recurrence. Post-rollback histograms look similar to pre-deploy.
sam-mlops: I'll run a quick smoke test hitting interactive endpoints with long token payloads to confirm token cap enforcement and batching behavior.
sam-mlops: smoke test results: requests >2048 tokens are rejected with 413, smaller requests processed with latency ~80-120ms. Good.
lina-support: Preparing a summary for customers: cause, mitigations, ETA for postmortem. Sending in 10m.
noah-runtime: Captured artifacts: logs tarball s3://redwood-incident-logs/1861203030/batcher-ws-logs.tgz, metrics snapshot s3://redwood-incident-metrics/1861203030-metrics.json, config diffs in PR #5402
sre-lead-jon: Assigning postmortem: eng-runtime, sam-mlops, alex-platform. Please include timeline and root cause (deploy -> larger tokens -> batch growth -> HOL -> timeouts). Include remediation: client SDK guardrails, gateway caps, safer batch defaults, and improved observability.
maria-oncall: Handoff note for next oncall: monitor queue_depth < 200 and error_rate < 1%. If either breaches for >10m, escalate to sre-lead-jon and rotate extra capacity (scale-up batcher nodes) and enable full fallback routing to rwd-llm-small-v1.
lina-support: Final customer note sent at T+40m. Customers onboarded to status page and updated tweets. No active SEV1 customers impacted; Chatly improved to acceptable SLAs.
eng-runtime-oncall: Marking this thread as incident active -> mitigated. Will update with postmortem link when created.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity=SEV2 -> mitigated; postmortem required. incident_id: INC-1861203030
maria-oncall: Thanks team. Good work executing quick config changes and customer comms. Going to sleep now — leaving monitoring enabled and will wake on any page.
eng-runtime-oncall: passing to next rotation in 25m. Closing this thread when postmortem created.
